newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police warn of rebel election violence.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police warn of rebel election violence.

text.p: Sri Lanka police have alerted political parties campaigning for this month's local government election to the possibility of Tamil rebel attacks, a senior police officer said on Monday.
"We have to be alert, since the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) can strike anywhere at any time," Colombo police chief D.M.T.B. Dissanayake told Reuters.
He said police officers throughout the country have been briefed and asked to be alert to the possiblity of LTTE attacks at crowded election meetings.
The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils on the predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island.

Some 18,000 candidates from 12 political parties, including the ruling coalition People's Alliance (PA), the main opposition United National Party (UNP) and 132 independent groups, will take part in the polls on March 21 for 238 local government bodies.
The degree of violence already associated with the election has risen to alarming proportions and could affect the fairness of the election, according to an independent monitoring group.

Paikiasothy Saravanamuttu of the Centre for Monitoring Election Violence said the group was appealing to all political parties to do whatever necessary to end the rising incidence of violence during the campaign.
The centre said nearly 500 incidents of election-related violence, mostly threats against candidates and their supporters, had been reported up to Friday.
The election has already been marred by the February 11 killing of a ruling party legislator in Ratnapura in central Sri Lanka.
Police said 17 suspects, including a UNP legislator and a former UNP mayor, are in custody over the killing, which sparked riots in Ratnapura.
Parliament speaker K.B. Ratnayake has called a second meeting between leaders of political parties contesting the election in a bid to end the violence.
At a meeting held early last week Ratnayake appealed to all leaders to exert tight control over their supporters.
